idiom_name: plain class over a dict standing in for the collaborator
implementation_notes: Duck typing means the fake is just an object with the same methods: a small class whose store is a dict satisfies the collaborator's protocol without any declaration, framework or generated code, so the classic structure is replaced by an ordinary object. unittest.mock is the tool for stubs and mocks (canned answers and call assertions), not for a working fake; use it only for the parts of the collaborator the fake does not implement. Pass the fake into the code under test and build a fresh one per test, and consider typing.Protocol to keep the fake's surface honest.
pitfalls: A mutable default argument (def __init__(self, users={})) or a module-level store makes the fake shared across tests - use None plus an instance-level dict.
The fake implements only the methods the current tests call, so protocol drift stays invisible until runtime; add a typing.Protocol or a contract test against the real adapter.
Returning None where the real repository raises (or the reverse) silently changes the error path the test is meant to exercise.
